# Configuration

<!-- GENERATED by `python -m scripts.dump_settings` from server/config.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

Where LTMS reads its settings depends on how it is deployed. Settings →
System status shows which one this server is.

| Deployment | Settings file | After editing |
|---|---|---|
| Docker Compose | `.env` next to `compose.yaml` | `docker compose up -d` (recreates the `ltms` container) |
| systemd service | `/etc/ltms/ltms.env` | restart the service (`systemctl restart ltms`) |

Every setting below is read when LTMS starts, so a change needs the restart
above. With Compose, every setting in this list is passed from `.env` to the
`ltms` container (`compose.yaml` lists them all; a test keeps that list
complete). Other services' values in `.env`, such as the LRS admin password,
are not passed to `ltms`.

Defaults come from `config/default.yaml`, then the code. A variable that is
unset or empty uses the default. Some settings can also be changed on the
dashboard: there, the dashboard's value wins unless the matching `*_LOCKED`
setting is true.

| Setting | Default | Also on the dashboard | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LTMS_DATABASE_URL` | (empty) |  | Full SQLAlchemy URL, e.g. `postgresql+asyncpg://user:pass@host:5432/ltms`. When set, it wins over the `LTMS_DB_*` parts. |
| `LTMS_DB_HOST` | `localhost` |  | PostgreSQL host, used when `LTMS_DATABASE_URL` is empty. |
| `LTMS_DB_PORT` | `5432` |  | PostgreSQL port, used when `LTMS_DATABASE_URL` is empty. |
| `LTMS_DB_NAME` | `ltms` |  | PostgreSQL database name, used when `LTMS_DATABASE_URL` is empty. |
| `LTMS_DB_USER` | `ltms` |  | PostgreSQL user, used when `LTMS_DATABASE_URL` is empty. |
| `LTMS_DB_PASSWORD` | (empty) |  | PostgreSQL password; required unless `LTMS_DATABASE_URL` is set. |
| `LTMS_SCHEMA_MODE` | `migrate` |  | Schema startup mode. "migrate" (the default) requires a PostgreSQL database to already be at the Alembic head and refuses to create tables; "create" runs create_all like the old behaviour. SQLite always uses create_all regardless of this mode. |
| `LTMS_ADMIN_USERNAME` | `admin` |  | The first admin account, created on the first start. |
| `LTMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD` | (empty) |  | That account's password (at least 16 characters), used only to create it. |
| `LTMS_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS` | `300` |  | Member bearer token lifetime |
| `LTMS_ADMIN_IDLE_MINUTES` | `60` | Settings → Admin sessions | Admin sessions (issue #378): a session ends after this many minutes without admin activity, or this many hours after sign-in, whichever comes first. These are defaults; Settings -> Admin sessions overrides them. |
| `LTMS_ADMIN_SESSION_MAX_HOURS` | `12` | Settings → Admin sessions | Admin sessions end this many hours after sign-in, active or not. |
| `LTMS_ADMIN_WARN_MINUTES` | `2` | Settings → Admin sessions | Minutes of warning before an idle admin session ends. |
| `LTMS_ADMIN_IDLE_MAX_MINUTES` | `480` |  | Site ceiling on the idle timeout, e.g. a STIG/ATO session-lock limit. The dashboard cannot set a longer idle timeout. |
| `LTMS_CHALLENGE_TTL_SECONDS` | `60` |  | /api/auth/challenge nonce lifetime |
| `LTMS_FUTURE_SKEW_SECONDS` | `300` |  | Reject record ts further than this in the future |
| `LTMS_COOKIE_SECURE` | `true` |  | Set false only for local http development |
| `LTMS_INGEST_RATE` | `10` |  | Global per-member ingest rate (records per second) across all members unless overridden per member. The default of 10 (~600 records/min) is the target for one robot on the fleet. |
| `LTMS_RECALL_RATE` | `5` |  | Recall requests/s |
| `LTMS_MAX_BATCH` | `100` |  | Records per POST /api/records |
| `LTMS_MAX_RECALL` | `200` |  | Records per GET /api/records |
| `LTMS_ENROLL_RATE_PER_IP` | `5` |  | Enroll requests per IP per hour |
| `LTMS_MAX_PENDING_ENROLLMENTS` | `20` |  | Refuse new enroll requests beyond this |
| `LTMS_RETENTION_PAYLOAD_RULES` | `[{"type":"event","days":90},{"type":"perception","days":90},{"tag":"telemetry","days":30}]` | Retention (unless `LTMS_RETENTION_LOCKED`) | Payload purge rules. Headers (summary, time, place, chain) are kept forever; only the payload (raw details) of a matching record is deleted after `days`. A rule matches on type, tag, or both. Records tagged `keep` are never purged. Policy and system payloads can't be purged. Env override, as JSON: LTMS_RETENTION_PAYLOAD_RULES='[{"tag":"telemetry","days":14}]' |
| `LTMS_RETENTION_AUDIT_DAYS` | `365` | Retention (unless `LTMS_RETENTION_LOCKED`) | Audit log rows older than this many days are deleted weekly (memory-wipe rows are always kept). |
| `LTMS_ADDRESS_HISTORY_DAYS` | `180` |  | Member addresses (#189): rows not seen for this many days are pruned nightly. |
| `LTMS_ENABLE_SCHEDULER` | `true` |  | Run the background jobs (retention, LRS forwarding, refreshes). Tests turn it off. |
| `LTMS_DASHBOARD_DIR` | (empty) |  | Optional: serve the built dashboard (dashboard/dist) from this process. Production uses nginx for static files; this is for local/LAN use. |
| `LTMS_SECRET_KEY` | (empty) |  | Secret used to encrypt LRS credentials at rest. Without it, endpoints can still be created, but none may store a secret. |
| `LTMS_LRS_BOOTSTRAP_URL` | (empty) |  | LRS bootstrap (issue #86): register an LRS endpoint from env on first start. Empty LTMS_LRS_BOOTSTRAP_URL disables bootstrapping entirely. |
| `LTMS_LRS_BOOTSTRAP_NAME` | `default-lrs` |  | Name of the bootstrapped LRS endpoint. |
| `LTMS_LRS_BOOTSTRAP_USERNAME` | (empty) |  | The bootstrapped endpoint's LRS key. |
| `LTMS_LRS_BOOTSTRAP_SECRET` | (empty) |  | The bootstrapped endpoint's LRS secret (needs `LTMS_SECRET_KEY`). |
| `LTMS_LRS_BOOTSTRAP_XAPI_VERSION` | `2.0.0` |  | XAPI version the bootstrapped endpoint speaks. |
| `LTMS_LRS_BOOTSTRAP_TYPES` | (empty) |  | Record types forwarded to the bootstrapped endpoint, comma-separated. |
| `LTMS_LRS_BOOTSTRAP_ENABLED` | `false` |  | Whether the bootstrapped endpoint starts enabled. |
| `LTMS_LRS_FORWARD_SECONDS` | `30` |  | LRS forwarding (issue #61): how often the forwarder runs, how many records per endpoint per run, and the public base URL put in translated statements. Empty LTMS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL disables forwarding (one warning per run, nothing sent). |
| `LTMS_LRS_BATCH_SIZE` | `50` |  | Records per batch sent to each LRS endpoint. |
| `LTMS_LRS_MAX_BATCHES_PER_RUN` | `20` |  | Keep sending until caught up, up to this many batches per endpoint per run |
| `LTMS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` | (empty) |  | Public address of this LTMS; the base of every xAPI statement IRI. Empty turns LRS forwarding off. |
| `LTMS_MCP_READ_MODE` | `off` | Access (unless `LTMS_MCP_SETTINGS_LOCKED`) | Remote MCP read access (issue #106): who may read records over MCP, and what they may read when no token is presented. off - read access is denied (default, closed). token - only a presented, valid mcp read token grants read scope. open - no token needed; the open scope (mcp_open_scope) applies. |
| `LTMS_MCP_OPEN_SCOPE` | `{"types":[],"swarms":null}` | Access (unless `LTMS_MCP_SETTINGS_LOCKED`) | The read scope granted when mode is "open" and no token is presented. JSON, e.g. {"types":["thought","lesson"],"swarms":["alpha"]}. Defaults are closed: an empty "types" list sees nothing. |
| `LTMS_MCP_SETTINGS_LOCKED` | `false` |  | When true, the environment (LTMS_MCP_READ_MODE / LTMS_MCP_OPEN_SCOPE) is authoritative: the dashboard-stored value is ignored, writes return 409 locked, and the Access page shows the settings read-only. For operators who want config-as-code. |
| `LTMS_ENROLLMENT_POLICY` | `manual` | Members (unless `LTMS_ENROLLMENT_POLICY_LOCKED`) | Enrollment request policy (issue #129): manual - requests wait for an admin (default). auto_deny - new requests are refused at once (403 enrollment_closed), except a valid invite for an invite-mode swarm. auto_approve- free-agent requests are approved at once with recall only. |
| `LTMS_ENROLLMENT_POLICY_LOCKED` | `false` |  | When true, the environment (LTMS_ENROLLMENT_POLICY) is authoritative: the dashboard-stored value is ignored, writes return 409 locked. |
| `LTMS_RETENTION_LOCKED` | `false` |  | LTMS_RETENTION_LOCKED: environment data retention settings win over the dashboard (#155) |
| `LTMS_DATA_DIR` | `./data` |  | Fleet datasets (#237): content-addressed files under <data_dir>/datasets. |
| `LTMS_FLEET_KEY_PATH` | (empty) |  | Fleet key (#303): signs directives. Default: <data_dir>/fleet-key.json, mode 0600. |
| `LTMS_DATASET_TEXT_MAX_MB` | `25` |  | Text and document dataset files are extracted up to this size (MB). |
| `LTMS_DATASET_UPLOAD_MAX_MB` | `500` |  | Largest file an upload may be (#245); above this, use a catalog integration. |
| `LTMS_DATASET_URL_ALLOW` | (empty) |  | URL datasets (#249): hosts LTMS may snapshot from, comma-separated, exact ("docs.ros.org") or "*.example.org". Empty (the default) means off. |
| `LTMS_LRS_MSG_SUMMARY_PER_HOUR` | `60` |  | Swarm-message summaries to the LRS (#301): a member that sent more than LTMS_LRS_MSG_SUMMARY_PER_HOUR swarm messages in each of the last LTMS_LRS_MSG_SUMMARY_SUSTAIN_HOURS clock hours has them sent as one statement per LTMS_LRS_MSG_SUMMARY_WINDOW_MINUTES window. LTMS keeps every message. |
| `LTMS_LRS_MSG_SUMMARY_SUSTAIN_HOURS` | `3` |  | Hours in a row a member must stay over the per-hour limit before its messages are summarised. |
| `LTMS_LRS_MSG_SUMMARY_WINDOW_MINUTES` | `5` |  | Each summary statement covers this many minutes of messages. |
| `LTMS_REFERENCE_REFRESH_HOURS` | `168` |  | Built-in reference sources (#351): once imported from the dashboard, LTMS checks each for a new publication this often (hours); 0 = never. New publications arrive as pending versions. |
| `LTMS_CHARTER_GRACE_DAYS` | `14` |  | Fleet charter (#255): days existing members have to read a new version before their writes pause. |
| `LTMS_GEOIP_DB` | (empty) |  | Optional offline city database for network location estimates (#191). Normally an admin turns estimates on in Settings, and LTMS keeps the file under <data_dir>/geoip/ (#388). When this is set it wins and the dashboard's controls are off. |
| `LTMS_GEOIP_REFRESH_DAYS` | `30` |  | In download mode, fetch a new DB-IP City Lite file this often (days); 0 = never (#388). |
| `LTMS_PENDING_ENROLLMENT_TTL_DAYS` | `14` |  | Pending enrollment requests older than this many days are expired by the hourly scheduler job. |
| `LTMS_DEPLOYMENT` | (empty) |  | How this server is deployed (#390): "docker" (the image sets it) or "service" (systemd). Empty means detect it. Settings -> System status shows it, so admins know which file holds the settings. |
